terms.comment: In Celsus and Ovid a spreading, eating sore, which the ancients could not cure; Traupman and Morgan–Owens give it for the disease. Its other senses are the crab and the constellation Cancer, and so the summer heat (Ov.). To have cancer: cancrō labōrāre or cancrō afficī (Traupman 64).

evidence: Cato Agr. 157.4; Cels. 5.28.2; Plin. NH 22.32 (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The Greek word, of which cancer is the Latin (Lewis & Short); the medical term.

phrases.latin: utque malum lātē solet inmedicābile cancer serpere et inlaesās vitiātīs addere partēs
phrases.english: and as an incurable cancer spreads far and wide and adds the healthy parts to the diseased

sources: Lewis & Short: cancer · Lewis & Short: carcinoma
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 63–64, 286. Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. cancer.
